Q0523

“Promises are the uniquely human way of ordering the future, making it…” — Hannah Arendt (The Human Condition (1958))

Verified English quotation. Primary source: The Human Condition (1958). Theme: responsibility.

Source and attribution

The archive attributes this English wording to The Human Condition (1958) and files it under Political Phenomenology. That locator distinguishes the passage from loose internet attributions: readers can return to the named work or section to check translation, surrounding argument, and edition-specific wording.

About Hannah Arendt

Hannah Arendt (1906–1975) was a German-Jewish political theorist who fled Nazism and wrote in the United States in English and German. A student of Heidegger and Jaspers, she refused the label “philosopher” yet produced lasting works on totalitarianism, revolution, and the vita activa.

How to read this passage

Philosophical debates cover free will, blame, collective responsibility, and duties to distant others. Technology and AI revive the question of who is accountable when systems act. This passage enters that discussion through responsibility, action, time.

Concepts in this quote

Responsibility
Responsibility asks what we answer for—our choices, omissions, institutions, and the futures we help create.
Action
Action concerns agency: what it is to do something intentionally, and how thought becomes practice.
Time
Philosophy of time asks what tense and duration are—and how memory, death, and history shape a human life.
